niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand awareness vs. direct-response), budget, geography, target audiences, creative needs, and whether you need full-service media + creative or a specialist programmatic partner. To help you pick, here’s a short, practical guide: top options by type, what to look for, and next steps.

Top options (by capability/type)
- Global, full-service media groups (good when you want scale, planning, cross-channel integration)
  - GroupM (Mindshare, Wavemaker, MediaCom) — deep programmatic + measurement capabilities.
  - Omnicom Media Group (OMD, PHD) — strategy, premium publisher relationships, creative integration.
  - Publicis Media (Starcom, Zenith, Spark Foundry) — strong data-driven planning and activation.
  - IPG Mediabrands (Initiative, UM) — analytics-forward, performance and reach orientation.

- Programmatic/CTV specialists and platforms (best for direct buying, technical proficiency, testing)
  - The Trade Desk — leading DSP used by many agencies for CTV buys (not an agency, but a core buying platform).
  - Amobee — cross-screen ad tech for TV + digital.
  - Cadent (Comcast) — addressable/linear-CTV planning and activation across MVPD/streaming inventory.
  - Tremor Video / Unruly — video DSPs with premium publisher relationships.
  - Roku Advertising, Samsung Ads — platform-direct buying and audience data on their devices.

- Creative and performance boutiques (good when you need CTV-specific creative + fast optimization)
  - VaynerMedia, Tinuiti, R/GA, 72andSunny, and other independent shops that offer CTV creative and media integration (sizing varies by market).

How to choose (key criteria)
- Inventory access: premium streaming publishers, device/platform access (Roku, Samsung, Hulu, Pluto, MVPDs).
- DSP & buying approach: programmatic open-market vs. private marketplaces vs. platform-direct.
- Measurement & attribution: independent measurement partners, cross-screen attribution, viewability/valid impressions.
- Targeting & data: first-/second-party data use, audience segmentation, privacy compliance.
- Creative capabilities: CTV-specific creative (long-form, frequency, sequential storytelling, dynamic creative).
- Transparency & fees: clear reporting, media transparency, ad fraud mitigation.
- Case studies & references: results for similar KPIs/industry.
- Technology & reporting cadence: dashboards, API access, real-time optimization.
- Geographic reach and language support if running international campaigns.

Suggested RFP / interview questions
- Show a recent CTV campaign case study with KPIs, media plan breakdown, and results.
- Which platforms and publishers will you access for my target audience?
- Which DSPs and measurement partners do you use?
- How do you handle creative optimization and A/B testing for CTV?
- How do you prevent fraud and ensure viewability?
- What are your fees and how is media billed?
- Who owns the data and reporting? How often do you report and what does the dashboard look like?
- Can you run a 4–6 week pilot/test and what would that cost?

Next steps
- Tell me your goals (brand vs. performance), monthly budget, target geography and audience, and whether you need creative + production. I can recommend 2–3 agencies that are the best fit and a sample brief to send them.
- If you already have DSP/platform preferences (e.g., The Trade Desk, Roku), say so — I’ll narrow recommendations accordingly.

If you want, I can shortlist 3 agencies now based on your specific campaign type and budget — what are you trying to accomplish and where?
